AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and N2 per binding rule 4. SandCastle.cs:22-32 upgrades exactly `base.DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue` == CardsVar(6) == SIX cards, chosen by StableShuffle over Rng.Niche; sand_castle.py:16-18 loops the whole deck. Wrong count (G1, LIVE) and an unconsumed named RNG stream (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port drops C#'s `.Take(CardsVar(6).IntValue)` and upgrades EVERY upgradable deck card
guards.issue: MECHANISM: SandCastle.cs:24-25 is `PileType.Deck.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(c => c?.IsUpgradable ?? false).ToList().StableShuffle(Owner.RunState.Rng.Niche).Take(base.DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue)`, and CanonicalVars pins `new CardsVar(6)` (SandCastle.cs:20) with no AscensionHelper branch anywhere in the file, so the non-ascension count is 6. sand_castle.py:16-18 is `for card in run.deck: if card.is_upgradable: card.upgrade()` -- no count, no shuffle, no stream. Its own docstring (sand_castle.py:8) states the wrong rule outright: 'upgrade ALL upgradable cards in the deck'. PROMPT.md bug class 19 in its purest form -- a wrong constant hidden behind a confident docstring, except here the constant is missing entirely. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b14.py sand-castle): the Ironclad starting deck is 10 cards and all 10 are upgradable, so `run.add_relic('sand_castle')` upgrades 10 where the game upgrades 6; the printed deck is [('bash', 1), ('defend', 1), ('strike', 1)]. Both sides ported and nothing further is needed: Sand Castle is one of the three OPTION_POOL_1 relics at the ported Orobas shrine (events/orobas.py:20), and every run reaches Orobas in act 2 with more than six upgradable cards. The divergence grows with deck size and is permanent -- the upgrades are on the run deck, and conformance/runner.py compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs. The sibling relics/fragrant_mushroom.py:24-40 implements the identical C# idiom correctly, which is why this is a defect and not a house style (PROMPT.md class 12's 'check whether a sibling already does the thing'). Rule 7: relics/fragrant_mushroom.py, run.py and conformance/runner.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: G2: `Rng.Niche` is named in C# and the sim consumes nothing (PROMPT.md bug class 16)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the choice of WHICH six cards comes from `StableShuffle(base.Owner.RunState.Rng.Niche)` (SandCastle.cs:24) -- a real draw, unlike the CardTransformation case class 16 warns about, because StableShuffle consumes one swap per element. sand_castle.py touches no RNG at all. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py sand-castle): with a parity rng_set attached, the Niche counter goes 0 -> 0 across add_relic('sand_castle'), while the sibling fragrant_mushroom moves it 0 -> 9 for its own StableShuffle. LIVE for RNG parity (any recorded seed that takes Sand Castle diverges both in the cards upgraded and in every later Niche draw -- monster unique-HP rolls, Fishing Rod, Neow's Bones curses), DORMANT for RL play, which is the same live/dormant split relic/astrolabe N1 recorded for the same mechanism. Filed separately from G1 because fixing the count without wiring the stream leaves this half broken. Rule 7: relics/fragrant_mushroom.py, actmap.py (stable_shuffle) and rng.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: `CardCmd.Upgrade(item, CardPreviewStyle.GridLayout)` (SandCastle.cs:29) vs the sim's bare `card.upgrade()` -- PROMPT.md bug class 14
guards.rationale: CardCmd.Upgrade skips cards whose IsUpgradable is false, and the sim's Card.upgrade() has no such guard -- but sand_castle.py:17 supplies it (`if card.is_upgradable`), mirroring the C# Where clause on line 24. So the class-14 exposure is closed at this site. py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-upgrade does not list sand_castle.py among its 7 unguarded call sites, and reading the body confirms it. Rule 7: cards/base.py is not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: C# builds the candidate list from `PileType.Deck` only; the sim iterates run.deck
guards.rationale: Both are the run's deck pile. The relic fires out of combat (after_obtained on the run), so there are no draw/discard/hand piles to confuse -- unlike relic/stone_cracker, whose C# counterpart deliberately reads the DRAW pile in combat. Recorded because getting the pile wrong is the other half of this idiom.

guards.what: N3: `undo_after_obtained` is not implemented, and the pickup mutates run state outside run.relics
guards.rationale: Per PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3, the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site: the helper has no C# counterpart -- nothing in the game un-picks a relic -- so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source. Flagged for its operational consequence only: Sand Castle's upgrades are deck mutations, so when the conformance runner grants a node's relic and then swaps it for the one the save records, the upgrades stay behind and the deck comparison reads high. That is a tooling defect, not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: relics/base.py:143-150 and conformance/runner.py are not hashed here.
